correctness.rationale: The nonzero affine recursion from fixed-point positions gives a unique initial knot for even branch count and one free initial knot for odd branch count. All exact two-cycle points arise from ordered distinct inverse-branch pairs, whose strict contraction and ordered intervals identify (1,2) as the leftmost; algebra yields q=p2*b1/(1-p2+b1). The open one-parameter odd fiber proves sharp necessity. 271 exact rational checks supplement (not replace) the universal proof; endpoints and shared knot boundaries are excluded from exact period two by their eventual endpoint behavior.

value.rationale: The source poses geometric reconstruction of an interval map from unmarked periodic orbits. The finite-data version is natural for exact identification within the canonical fully expanding variable-knot zigzag family. The theorem *completely classifies* the fibers under period-one data, reveals a parity obstruction, and resolves it at the provably minimal period by a single geometrically selected unlabelled point, uniformly for all branch counts. It is not a numerical recomputation or a mere restatement of full-spectrum uniqueness; it does not claim stability under noise or unrestricted map classes.
